name: Kalanggaman Island
blurb: A long white sandbar with clear water on both sides.
about: Kalanggaman is a small uninhabited island off Palompon, famous for the two sandbars that stretch out from either end into clear turquoise water. The local government manages visits to protect the island, so it stays clean and uncrowded.
highlights: Twin sandbars that change shape with the tide
Swimming and snorkeling in clear shallow water
Picnic and cottage area under the trees
Sunset views over the Camotes Sea
best: March to May, when the sea is usually calm. Arrive early for the best light and fewer people.
getThere: Take a boat from the Palompon port. The crossing depends on sea conditions, so book through the tourism office.
tip: Bring your own food and water, and take your trash back with you. Daily visitor numbers are managed, so book ahead.

name: Cuatro Islas
blurb: Small islands with white sand and calm coves for a day trip.
about: Cuatro Islas is a group of four islands off Inopacan (Himokilan, Mahaba, Apid and Digyo), each with its own character. Expect white sand, rock formations, clear water and quiet coves ideal for island hopping.
highlights: Island hopping between the four islands
Snorkeling over coral and clear shallows
White sand coves for swimming and picnics
best: Dry, calm months (roughly March to May). Go in the morning when the water is flat.
getThere: Travel to Inopacan, then take a boat from the town's landing point. Boats and guides can be arranged locally.
tip: Bring sun protection and cash for boat rental and fees. Ask your boatman about weather before setting out.

name: Lake Danao Natural Park
blurb: A guitar-shaped mountain lake with cool air and morning mist.
about: Lake Danao sits high in the mountains above Ormoc and is known for its guitar shape. The park is cool, quiet and green, with a calm lake surrounded by forest.
highlights: Kayaking and bamboo raft rides on the lake
Short forest walks and lakeside picnics
Cool mountain air and morning mist
best: Morning, before the mist clears. Dry months give the most reliable weather.
getThere: Travel from Ormoc City by road up into the mountains. Motorbikes, vans and hired vehicles make the trip.
tip: It gets cool and damp, so bring a light jacket. Weekdays are quieter than weekends.

name: Mahagnao Volcano Natural Park
blurb: Forest trails around a crater lake.
about: Mahagnao is a protected natural park around a dormant volcano in Burauen, with a crater lake and forest trails. It suits hikers and campers who want a quiet, green escape.
best: Morning, in the dry months. Trails can be slippery after rain.
getThere: Travel to Burauen by road, then continue to the park entrance. Ask the park office about guides.
tip: Wear shoes with good grip and register at the entrance. Start early so you finish before dark.

name: Mount Pangasugan
blurb: A forested mountain in the Leyte range, known for hiking trails.
about: Mount Pangasugan rises above Baybay City in the Leyte mountain range. It is a popular hiking destination with forested slopes and cool air.
best: Early morning start in dry weather, so you are off the trail before afternoon rain.
getThere: Travel to Baybay City, then continue to the trailhead with a local guide.
tip: A guide is required. Bring water, rain protection and a headlamp if you plan to camp.

name: San Juanico Bridge
blurb: The long bridge linking Leyte and Samar, best at first light.
about: San Juanico Bridge crosses the San Juanico Strait between Leyte and Samar. At over two kilometers long, it is among the longest bridges in the Philippines and one of the region's best-known landmarks.
highlights: Long crossing between Leyte and Samar
Viewing deck near the Tacloban side
Free to visit at any hour
best: Sunrise or late afternoon, when the light is soft and the heat is lower.
getThere: Take a jeepney, tricycle or taxi from Tacloban City toward the bridge. Parking is available near the viewing deck.
tip: Take care near the road and watch for traffic. Go at first light for the best photos.

name: MacArthur Landing Memorial National Park
blurb: Statues on the shore of Leyte Gulf mark the 1944 landing.
about: This park in Palo marks the place where General Douglas MacArthur and Philippine leaders waded ashore on October 20, 1944, starting the liberation of the country. Life-size statues show the moment on the shore of Leyte Gulf.
best: Morning, before the heat builds. October 20 is the anniversary of the landing.
getThere: Palo is a short ride south of Tacloban City by jeepney, van or tricycle.
tip: Pair it with Palo Metropolitan Cathedral for a half-day history trip.

name: Palo Metropolitan Cathedral
blurb: A centuries-old church in Palo, close to the landing memorial.
about: Palo Metropolitan Cathedral is a centuries-old church at the center of Palo. It was used as a field hospital during the 1944 Leyte campaign and remains an active place of worship.
highlights: Historic church with a long local history
best: Morning or late afternoon. Check mass times if you want to see the interior quietly.
getThere: In Palo town center, a short ride from Tacloban City by jeepney or tricycle.
tip: Dress modestly and keep quiet during services.

name: Santo Niño Shrine and Heritage Museum
blurb: A heritage museum and shrine in the city center.
about: This grand building in Tacloban City houses a museum of art, antiques and heritage displays, along with a collection of Santo Niño images. It is known for its large, ornate interiors.
best: Weekday mornings for a quieter visit. The museum is closed on Mondays.
getThere: In Tacloban City, reachable by tricycle or taxi from the city center.
tip: Ask for a guided tour to get the stories behind the collection.

name: Price Mansion
blurb: A historic mansion in Tacloban tied to the 1944 Leyte campaign.
about: Price Mansion is a historic house in Tacloban City built in the early 1900s. It is linked to the 1944 Leyte campaign, when American forces used it as a headquarters.
highlights: Short visit close to other city sights
getThere: In Tacloban City, a short tricycle or taxi ride from the center.
tip: Combine it with the Santo Niño Shrine for a city heritage tour.

name: Ormoc City Boulevard
blurb: A seaside promenade on Ormoc Bay for an evening walk.
about: Ormoc City Boulevard is a seaside promenade along Ormoc Bay. Locals come here in the late afternoon to walk, eat street food and watch the sun set over the water.
best: Late afternoon into evening, when the air cools and the sky turns gold.
getThere: In Ormoc City, a short tricycle ride from the city center.
tip: Bring small change for street food and arrive about an hour before sunset.

name: Victor’s Peak
blurb: A scenic, beginner-friendly day hike offering a panoramic view of Tacloban City and the iconic San Juanico Strait.
about: As the highest peak structure fully nestled within the city limits, Victor’s Peak stands at approximately 335 meters above sea level. It provides a fantastic escape for outdoor enthusiasts seeking an immediate inland nature retreat. The forested trails are rich with shade-giving trees, leading hikers up to a ridge summit that commands sweeping views over the urban cityscape, rolling hills, and the historic waters below. It is famously scaled as a standalone day trek or as part of the popular "Tacloban Tri-Peak" traverse alongside Mt. Carmel and Mt. Naga-Naga.
highlights: • Panoramic summit views of the San Juanico Strait
• Expansive urban landscape view overlooking Tacloban City
• Connecting ridge trails for a multi-mountain trilogy hike
getThere: • By Public Transit / Commute: From downtown Tacloban, ride an Apitong-bound jeepney or hail a local tricycle/motorcycle taxi and ask to be dropped off along the Brgy. Apitong Bypass Road near the Smashzone curve. • Trailheads: The main direct trailhead starts just past the curve on the left side of the bypass road. Alternatively, seasoned hikers can access it via a back-trail traverse starting from Mt. Carmel or the Mt. Naga-Naga trailhead.
tip: • Wear proper footwear: The trail can be steep or slick, so sturdy trail shoes or hiking sandals with good grip are highly recommended. • Mind the wildlife: The mountain's native name (Mt. Tubakon) references the local inch-long ants found near the summit flora, so stay mindful of where you step or sit! • Hydration: Bring at least 1–2 liters of water since there are no commercial convenience stalls along the direct trail climb. • Leave No Trace: Ensure you pack out all trash to help preserve the
